note: Coordinates place sites on an INTERNAL map — a scholarly reconstruction of relative geography from ~550 textual distance/direction clues (after Sorenson, Clark, and the BYU internal-model tradition). It is deliberately not a map of the Americas; no real-world location is implied.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.desc: The covenant city where the record begins, c. 600 BC, in the first year of King Zedekiah — soon to fall to Babylon, exactly as Lehi prophesied.

places.name: Valley of Lemuel
places.desc: Lehi's first wilderness camp near the Red Sea, with a river 'continually running' — where Lehi pled that Lemuel be firm and steadfast like the valley.

places.name: Nahom
places.desc: 'The place which was called Nahom,' where Ishmael was buried and the daughters mourned. A tribal area NHM in Yemen matching this name and era is one of the record's most discussed correlations.

places.name: Bountiful (Old World)
places.desc: The verdant seashore land of 'much fruit and wild honey' by the sea Irreantum, where Nephi built the ship. Candidate sites lie on the Oman coast.

places.name: Land of First Inheritance
places.desc: Where Lehi's party landed and first planted — on the west coast of the land southward. Later the heart of Lamanite country.

places.name: City of Nephi (Lehi-Nephi)
places.desc: Nephi's highland settlement and temple city, later lost to the Lamanites, re-colonized by Zeniff, and the stage for Noah, Abinadi, and Limhi.

places.name: Shilom
places.desc: Neighboring land to the city of Nephi, overlooked by the hill where King Noah built his tower to watch for Lamanite armies.

places.name: Shemlon
places.desc: Lamanite land bordering Nephi — where the daughters of the Lamanites gathered to sing and dance, and where watchtowers looked out from Noah's palaces.

places.name: Waters of Mormon
places.desc: The forest-hidden fountain where Alma baptized about 204 souls — 'how beautiful are they to the eyes of them who there came to the knowledge of their Redeemer.'

places.name: Helam
places.desc: The city Alma's people built eight days' journey from the waters of Mormon — where the Lord made their Amulonite burdens light before delivering them.

places.name: Land of Ishmael
places.desc: King Lamoni's kingdom, where Ammon kept the king's flocks and the great Lamanite conversion began.

places.name: Middoni
places.desc: Where Aaron and his brethren lay in prison until Lamoni and Ammon obtained their release from king Antiomno.

places.name: Narrow Strip of Wilderness
places.desc: The east–west mountain wilderness dividing Lamanite Nephi (south, higher) from Nephite Zarahemla (north, lower) — armies always go 'up' to Nephi and 'down' to Zarahemla.

places.name: Manti
places.desc: Southern frontier city near the head of the river Sidon — gateway of invasion routes and scene of Helaman's decisive stratagem with his stripling soldiers.

places.name: Zarahemla
places.desc: Capital of the Nephite nation for most of the record — seat of kings and judges, city of Benjamin's tower, Nephi's garden, and Samuel's wall.

places.name: River Sidon
places.desc: The record's only named river, rising in the southern wilderness and flowing north past Zarahemla to the sea. Site of the Amlicite and Zerahemnah battles.

places.name: Gideon
places.desc: Valley and city east of the river Sidon, named for the patriot who resisted King Noah — a righteous city where Alma found the church firm.

places.name: Minon
places.desc: Land above Zarahemla up the course of the Sidon, where Amlicite and Lamanite armies joined.

places.name: Melek
places.desc: Land west of Sidon by the borders of the wilderness, where Alma taught and the people of Ammon later settled before Jershon.

places.name: Ammonihah
places.desc: The proud city of Nehor's order that burned the believers — destroyed by the Lamanites in one day, 'the desolation of Nehors.'

places.name: City of Noah
places.desc: Neighbor of Ammonihah where the Lamanite invaders were finally repulsed after Ammonihah's fall.

places.name: Jershon
places.desc: The land the Nephites gave the people of Ammon 'for an inheritance,' guarded by Nephite armies — east by the sea, south of Bountiful.

places.name: Antionum
places.desc: Land of the Zoramites and their Rameumptom, east of Sidon, south of Jershon — Alma's mission field and later Lamanite staging ground.

places.name: Nephihah
places.desc: City in the southeast plains joining Moroni and Aaron — captured by the Lamanites and retaken when Moroni's men scaled the wall by night on ropes.

places.name: City of Moroni
places.desc: Fortified city by the east sea on the south border, first of Captain Moroni's new cities — later sunk in the sea at the crucifixion.

places.name: Mulek
places.desc: East-coast city named for Zedekiah's son; scene of Moroni and Lehi's perfect pincer trap that retook it without a single Nephite death in the decoy.

places.name: Bountiful
places.desc: The strategic land guarding the narrow neck — its fortified line kept the Lamanites from the land northward, and at its temple the risen Christ appeared.

places.name: Narrow Neck of Land
places.desc: The isthmus — 'a day and a half's journey for a Nephite' — joining the lands southward and northward; Hagoth launched his ships by it.

places.name: Land of Desolation
places.desc: The land northward, strewn with Jaredite bones and ruins when Limhi's explorers found it — later the Nephites' final retreat.

places.name: Hill Cumorah / Ramah
places.desc: The hill of two endings: Ramah, where the Jaredites destroyed themselves; Cumorah, where Mormon hid the records and the Nephite nation fell, AD 385.

places.name: Moron (Jaredite Seat)
places.desc: Royal land of the Jaredite kings, 'near the land called Desolation by the Nephites' — the stage for most of Ether's rise-and-fall chronicle.

places.name: Hagoth's Shipyard
places.desc: On the borders of Bountiful by the west sea, the 'exceedingly curious man' built ships that carried emigrants northward — some never heard of again.
